task.title: Three branches for the portfolio
task.description:
You are in the ~/portfolio folder on the main branch, the history has 3 commits, and the heading in index.html has a typo: Ana instead of Anna. Write the commands one per line: 1) Look at the list of branches. 2) Create the feature/contacts branch from main and switch to it with one command. 3) Create the file contacts.html with the text

Contacts

and commit it. 4) Append the line

Email: anna@example.com

to contacts.html and make the second commit. 5) Go back to main and create the fix/titel branch (exactly with the typo in the name), switching to it. 6) Overwrite index.html with two lines:

Anna Karimova

and

Frontend developer

- and make a commit. 7) Rename the fix/titel branch to fix/title. 8) Go back to main, create the experiment branch, overwrite style.css with the line body { background: black; } and make a commit. 9) Go back to main and delete the experiment branch (it is not merged - you will need to force the deletion). 10) Look at the graph of all branches (git log --oneline --graph --all) and at git status. At the end you are on main, the repository has exactly three branches: main, feature/contacts, fix/title, the working directory is clean, and main itself has not changed.

hints: Create a branch and switch to it at once: git switch -c feature/contacts. A plain git branch name creates the branch but does not switch to it.
A new file must be added before the first commit: git add contacts.html. The second commit can be made with git commit -am.
Create every new branch from main: first git switch main, then git switch -c name.
Rename the current branch: git branch -m fix/title - run it while you are on fix/titel.
git branch -d experiment will refuse to delete an unmerged branch (not fully merged). To force it: git branch -D experiment. You cannot delete the branch you are on - first git switch main.

questions.question: What is a branch in Git?
options: A full copy of all project files in a separate folder
A movable pointer (bookmark) to a commit
questions.explanation: A branch is just a name that points to a commit. Creating a branch means writing a new bookmark, no files are copied.

questions.question:
What did Git print?

$ git branch
  feature/contacts
* main
  fix/title
options: You are on the feature/contacts branch
You are on the main branch, there are three branches in total
main is the only branch with commits
questions.explanation: The asterisk * marks the current branch - the one HEAD points to.

questions.question: Enter the whole command: create the feature/menu branch and switch to it at once (with the modern command).
questions.explanation: git switch -c = git branch feature/menu + git switch feature/menu. The old form is git checkout -b feature/menu.

questions.question: Match the command with the result.
pairs: Delete a branch if its commits are already merged
Force-delete a branch, even with unmerged commits
Go back to the previous branch
questions.explanation: -d is a safe deletion, -D is a forced one, -m is renaming (move), switch - jumps back like cd -.

questions.question: You are on main. You ran git branch feature/blog and made a commit right away. Where will the commit be?
questions.explanation: git branch only creates a branch and does not switch to it. HEAD still points to main, so the commit goes there.

questions.question:
What did Git print?

$ git branch -d experiment
error: the branch 'experiment' is not fully merged
hint: If you are sure you want to delete it, run 'git branch -D experiment'
options: The branch is not deleted: it has commits that are not in the current branch
The experiment branch does not exist
You must switch to experiment first
questions.explanation: -d protects you from losing work. If you really do not need the commits - git branch -D experiment.

questions.question: You are on feature/contacts, where contacts.html is committed. You ran git switch main. What will happen?
options: contacts.html will disappear from the working directory
The commits of the feature/contacts branch will be deleted
The files in the folder will be as in the last commit of main
questions.explanation: Switching makes the files in the folder match the snapshot of the other branch. The commits of feature/contacts stay in the repository - go back to the branch, and the file appears again.

questions.question: You changed style.css (without committing) on main and ran git switch feature/contacts. style.css is the same in both branches. What will happen?
options: An error: commit the changes first
The switch will work, and the change in style.css will move with you
Git will make a commit automatically
questions.explanation: Uncommitted changes belong to the working directory, not to a branch. If the file is the same in the branches, Git carries the changes over. The would be overwritten error happens when the file differs between the branches.

questions.question:
What did Git print?

$ git status
HEAD detached at c0adb88
options: HEAD points right to a commit, not to a branch
questions.explanation: A detached HEAD means you are looking at an old commit. To go back: git switch main; to keep the commits made here: git switch -c new-branch.

questions.question: Which branch names are good according to the common rules?
questions.explanation: Latin letters, lowercase, hyphens instead of spaces, a feature/ or fix/ prefix. Git does not accept spaces at all: is not a valid branch name.

questions.question: Match the old git checkout command with the modern one.
questions.explanation: checkout can do everything at once, so it was split into switch (branches) and restore (files). You will meet the old form in other people's instructions.

questions.question: Enter the whole command: show the one-line history of all branches with a graph.
questions.explanation: --all shows all branches, not only the current one; --graph shows the branch lines on the left; --oneline shows each commit on one line.
